#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tau Launcher — modular, multi-user, multi-LLM
#
# Collapse chain (first hit wins):
#   1. $TAU_BIN (explicit override)
#   2. Installed `tau` on PATH (not this script — avoids recursion)
#   3. ./tau in current directory (local project override; regular file only)
#   4. Full compiled binary: <engine>/packages/coding-agent/dist/omp
#      (hermetic. 2026-09-20 tau-config: promoted above bun source mode.)
#   5. Source mode: bun run <engine>/packages/coding-agent/src/cli.ts
#      (dev fallback -- patches take effect immediately)
#
# Launcher-native subcommands (handled before the collapse chain):
#   tau vendor ...   upstream patch workflow
#   tau audit        read-only hyper-fix audit of config, skills, engine, bridge
#   tau tmux ...     tmux session management for parallel experiments
# Helpers live next to this script (tau-audit.sh, tau-tmux.sh).
#
# Profiles: $HOME/.tau/profiles/<name>.yml
#   Each profile selects LLM backend, model, and engine args.
#   Use --profile <name> or TAU_PROFILE env.
#
# Locking: flock on $HOME/.tau/.launcher.lock prevents concurrent
#   state-corrupting runs. Held only during startup/migration, not
#   for the whole session.
#
# Migrations: profile schema versioned. On load, if profile version
#   < CURRENT_SCHEMA, migrate forward automatically.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

# ── HOME resolution (multi-user) ──────────────────────────────────────
# Never hardcode /home/toxic. Respect $HOME; the bridge sometimes runs
# with HOME=/home/hatch even as user toxic, so fall back to the real
# user's home via getent when $HOME looks wrong.
resolve_home() {
    local h="${HOME:-}"
    if [ -n "$h" ] && [ -d "$h/.tau" ]; then
        printf '%s' "$h"
        return
    fi
    local user_home
    user_home="$(getent passwd "${USER:-$(id -un)}" 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f6)"
    if [ -n "$user_home" ] && [ -d "$user_home" ]; then
        printf '%s' "$user_home"
        return
    fi
    printf '%s' "${h:-/home/toxic}"
}
TAU_HOME="$(resolve_home)"
export TAU_HOME

TAU_DIR="$TAU_HOME/.tau"
PROFILES_DIR="$TAU_DIR/profiles"
LOCK_FILE="$TAU_DIR/.launcher.lock"
CURRENT_SCHEMA=2

mkdir -p "$PROFILES_DIR"

# ── Secrets (per-user) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
set +u
[ -f "$TAU_HOME/.secrets" ] && { set -a; . "$TAU_HOME/.secrets" >/dev/null 2>&1; set +a; }
[ -f "$TAU_HOME/.config/claude/env" ] && { set -a; . "$TAU_HOME/.config/claude/env" >/dev/null 2>&1; set +a; }
set -u

# 18.2.6 engine joins PI_CONFIG_DIR onto homedir (dirs.ts); absolute path doubles to /home/toxic/home/toxic/.tau. Keep as bare name.
export PI_CONFIG_DIR=".tau"

# ── Profile loading + migration ───────────────────────────────────────
TAU_PROFILE="${TAU_PROFILE:-default}"
# Allow --profile <name> as first arg
if [ "${1:-}" = "--profile" ] && [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
    TAU_PROFILE="$2"
    shift 2
fi

migrate_profile() {
    local profile_file="$1"
    local version
    version="$(rg 'schema_version:' "$profile_file" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's/.*schema_version:[[:space:]]*//' | awk '{print $1}' || true)"
    version="${version:-1}"

    if [ "$version" -lt "$CURRENT_SCHEMA" ]; then
        # v1 → v2: add llm.backend field, default to auto
        if [ "$version" -eq 1 ]; then
            if ! rg -q 'backend:' "$profile_file" 2>/dev/null; then
                printf '\nllm:\n  backend: auto\n' >> "$profile_file"
            fi
            # Bump version marker
            if rg -q 'schema_version:' "$profile_file" 2>/dev/null; then
                sed -i 's/schema_version:\s*[0-9]*/schema_version: 2/' "$profile_file"
            else
                printf 'schema_version: 2\n' >> "$profile_file"
            fi
        fi
    fi
}

load_profile() {
    local profile_file="$PROFILES_DIR/$TAU_PROFILE.yml"
    if [ ! -f "$profile_file" ]; then
        # Create default profile on first run
        cat > "$profile_file" <<'EOF'
schema_version: 2
# LLM backend: auto | anthropic | openai | kimi | ollama
llm:
  backend: auto
  model: null
engine:
  args: []
EOF
    fi

    # Migrate under lock
    (
        flock -w 10 200 || { echo "tau: could not acquire profile lock" >&2; exit 1; }
        migrate_profile "$profile_file"
    ) 200>"$LOCK_FILE"

    # Export profile settings as env (portable parsing, no PCRE)
    local backend
    backend="$(rg 'backend:' "$profile_file" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's/.*backend:[[:space:]]*//' | awk '{print $1}' || true)"
    backend="${backend:-auto}"
    export TAU_LLM_BACKEND="$backend"

    local model
    model="$(rg '^[[:space:]]*model:' "$profile_file" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's/.*model:[[:space:]]*//' | awk '{print $1}' || true)"
    if [ -n "$model" ] && [ "$model" != "null" ]; then
        export TAU_LLM_MODEL="$model"
    fi
}

load_profile

# ── Engine resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Sovereign checkout location (also HOME-aware)
SOVEREIGN_DIR="$TAU_HOME/sovereign"
# Primary: projects/tau (first-class), fallback: tau/engine (compat symlink)
if [ -d "$SOVEREIGN_DIR/projects/tau/engine" ]; then
    ENGINE_DIR="$SOVEREIGN_DIR/projects/tau/engine"
else
    ENGINE_DIR="$SOVEREIGN_DIR/tau/engine"
fi
ENGINE_ENTRY="$ENGINE_DIR/packages/coding-agent/src/cli.ts"
DIST_BIN="$ENGINE_DIR/packages/coding-agent/dist/omp"

# Vendor update commands (run before engine launch)
vendor_cmd() {
    local subcmd="${1:-}"
    local ROOT="$SOVEREIGN_DIR/projects/tau"
    local UPSTREAM_DIR="$ROOT/upstream-changes"
    local SCRIPTS_DIR="$UPSTREAM_DIR/scripts"

    case "$subcmd" in
        update|fetch|ingest)
            echo "Fetching upstream changes..."
            "$SCRIPTS_DIR/ingest.sh"
            ;;
        status)
            "$SCRIPTS_DIR/status.sh"
            ;;
        promote)
            local patch="${2:-}"
            if [ -z "$patch" ]; then
                echo "Usage: tau vendor promote <patches/*.patch>"
                exit 1
            fi
            "$SCRIPTS_DIR/promote.sh" "$patch"
            ;;
        build)
            echo "Building coding-agent binary..."
            cd "$ROOT/engine/packages/coding-agent" && bun run scripts/build-binary.ts
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Usage: tau vendor {update|status|promote|build}"
            echo "  update   - Fetch upstream changes and generate patches"
            echo "  status   - Show pending patches and upstream status"
            echo "  promote  - Apply a patch (tau vendor promote <patch>)"
            echo "  build    - Build the coding-agent binary"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
}

# Collapse chain
launch() {
    # Handle vendor subcommand first
    if [ "${1:-}" = "vendor" ]; then
        vendor_cmd "${2:-}"
        return
    fi

    # Launcher-native subcommands: audit + tmux (helpers beside this script)
    if [ "${1:-}" = "audit" ]; then
        shift
        if [ -x "$SCRIPT_DIR/tau-audit.sh" ]; then
            exec "$SCRIPT_DIR/tau-audit.sh" "$@"
        else
            echo "tau: tau-audit.sh not found beside $0" >&2
            echo "  reinstall from sovereign/projects/tau/launcher/" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    if [ "${1:-}" = "tmux" ]; then
        shift
        if [ -x "$SCRIPT_DIR/tau-tmux.sh" ]; then
            exec "$SCRIPT_DIR/tau-tmux.sh" "$@"
        else
            echo "tau: tau-tmux.sh not found beside $0" >&2
            echo "  reinstall from sovereign/projects/tau/launcher/" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    fi

    # 1. Explicit override
    if [ -n "${TAU_BIN:-}" ] && [ -x "$TAU_BIN" ]; then
        exec "$TAU_BIN" "$@"
    fi

    # 2. Installed tau on PATH (guard against self-recursion)
    local path_tau
    path_tau="$(command -v tau 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -n "$path_tau" ] && [ "$path_tau" != "$0" ] && [ -x "$path_tau" ]; then
        # Avoid infinite loop: only use if it's not this script
        if ! rg -q "Tau Launcher — modular" "$path_tau" 2>/dev/null; then
            exec "$path_tau" "$@"
        fi
    fi

    # 3. Local ./tau override (regular file only — a ./tau directory must not match -x)
    if [ -f "./tau" ] && [ -x "./tau" ] && [ "$(realpath ./tau 2>/dev/null)" != "$(realpath "$0" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        exec ./tau "$@"
    fi

    # 4. Full compiled binary first (hermetic; see header)
    if [ -x "$DIST_BIN" ]; then
        exec "$DIST_BIN" "$@"
    fi

    # 5. Source mode fallback (bun) -- dev
    if [ -f "$ENGINE_ENTRY" ] && command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        exec bun run "$ENGINE_ENTRY" "$@"
    fi

    echo "tau: no launch target found" >&2
    echo "  checked: TAU_BIN, PATH, ./tau" >&2
    echo "  checked: $ENGINE_ENTRY (bun: $(command -v bun || echo missing))" >&2
    echo "  checked: $DIST_BIN" >&2
    exit 1
}

launch "$@"

    local profile_file="$1"

    local SCRIPTS_DIR="$UPSTREAM_DIR/scripts"

    case "$subcmd" in
        update|fetch|ingest)
            echo "Fetching upstream changes..."
            "$SCRIPTS_DIR/ingest.sh"
            ;;
        status)
            "$SCRIPTS_DIR/status.sh"

        promote)
            local patch="${2:-}"
            if [ -z "$patch" ]; then
                echo "Usage: tau vendor promote <patches/*.patch>"

            fi
            "$SCRIPTS_DIR/promote.sh" "$patch"
            ;;
        build)
            echo "Building coding-agent binary..."
            cd "$ROOT/engine/packages/coding-agent" && bun run scripts/build-binary.ts
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Usage: tau vendor {update|status|promote|build}"
            echo "  update   - Fetch upstream changes and generate patches"
            echo "  status   - Show pending patches and upstream status"
            echo "  promote  - Apply a patch (tau vendor promote <patch>)"
            echo "  build    - Build the coding-agent binary"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
}

# Collapse chain
launch() {
    # Handle vendor subcommand first
    if [ "${1:-}" = "vendor" ]; then
        vendor_cmd "${2:-}"
        return
    fi

    # Launcher-native subcommands: audit + tmux (helpers beside this script)
    if [ "${1:-}" = "audit" ]; then
        shift
        if [ -x "$SCRIPT_DIR/tau-audit.sh" ]; then
            exec "$SCRIPT_DIR/tau-audit.sh" "$@"
        else
            echo "tau: tau-audit.sh not found beside $0" >&2
            echo "  reinstall from sovereign/projects/tau/launcher/" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    if [ "${1:-}" = "tmux" ]; then
        shift
        if [ -x "$SCRIPT_DIR/tau-tmux.sh" ]; then
            exec "$SCRIPT_DIR/tau-tmux.sh" "$@"
        else
            echo "tau: tau-tmux.sh not found beside $0" >&2
            echo "  reinstall from sovereign/projects/tau/launcher/" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    fi

    # 1. Explicit override
    if [ -n "${TAU_BIN:-}" ] && [ -x "$TAU_BIN" ]; then
        exec "$TAU_BIN" "$@"
    fi

    # 2. Installed tau on PATH (guard against self-recursion)
    local path_tau
    path_tau="$(command -v tau 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -n "$path_tau" ] && [ "$path_tau" != "$0" ] && [ -x "$path_tau" ]; then
        # Avoid infinite loop: only use if it's not this script
        if ! rg -q "Tau Launcher — modular" "$path_tau" 2>/dev/null; then
            exec "$path_tau" "$@"
        fi
    fi

    # 3. Local ./tau override (regular file only — a ./tau directory must not match -x)
    if [ -f "./tau" ] && [ -x "./tau" ] && [ "$(realpath ./tau 2>/dev/null)" != "$(realpath "$0" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        exec ./tau "$@"
    fi

    # 4. Full compiled binary first (hermetic; see header)
    if [ -x "$DIST_BIN" ]; then
        exec "$DIST_BIN" "$@"
    fi

    # 5. Source mode fallback (bun) -- dev
    if [ -f "$ENGINE_ENTRY" ] && command -v bun >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        exec bun run "$ENGINE_ENTRY" "$@"
    fi

    echo "tau: no launch target found" >&2
    echo "  checked: TAU_BIN, PATH, ./tau" >&2
    echo "  checked: $ENGINE_ENTRY (bun: $(command -v bun || echo missing))" >&2
    echo "  checked: $DIST_BIN" >&2
    exit 1
}

launch "$@"

# Test-Driven Development

## Philosophy

**Core principle**: Tests should verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't.

**Good tests** are integration-style: they exercise real code paths through public APIs. They describe _what_ the system does, not _how_ it does it. A good test reads like a specification - "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists. These tests survive refactors because they don't care about internal structure.

**Bad tests** are coupled to implementation. They mock internal collaborators, test private methods, or verify through external means (like querying a database directly instead of using the interface). The warning sign: your test breaks when you refactor, but behavior hasn't changed. If you rename an internal function and tests fail, those tests were testing implementation, not behavior.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Anti-Pattern: Horizontal Slices

**DO NOT write all tests first, then all implementation.** This is "horizontal slicing" - treating RED as "write all tests" and GREEN as "write all code."

This produces **crap tests**:

- Tests written in bulk test _imagined_ behavior, not _actual_ behavior
- You end up testing the _shape_ of things (data structures, function signatures) rather than user-facing behavior
- Tests become insensitive to real changes - they pass when behavior breaks, fail when behavior is fine
- You outrun your headlights, committing to test structure before understanding the implementation

**Correct approach**: Vertical slices via tracer bullets. One test → one implementation → repeat. Each test responds to what you learned from the previous cycle. Because you just wrote the code, you know exactly what behavior matters and how to verify it.

```
WRONG (horizontal):
  RED:   test1, test2, test3, test4, test5
  GREEN: impl1, impl2, impl3, impl4, impl5

RIGHT (vertical):
  RED→GREEN: test1→impl1
  RED→GREEN: test2→impl2
  RED→GREEN: test3→impl3
  ...
```

## Workflow

### 1. Planning

Before writing any code:

- [ ] Confirm with user what interface changes are needed
- [ ] Confirm with user which behaviors to test (prioritize)
- [ ] Identify opportunities for [deep modules](deep-modules.md) (small interface, deep implementation)
- [ ] Design interfaces for [testability](interface-design.md)
- [ ] List the behaviors to test (not implementation steps)
- [ ] Get user approval on the plan

Ask: "What should the public interface look like? Which behaviors are most important to test?"

**You can't test everything.** Confirm with the user exactly which behaviors matter most. Focus testing effort on critical paths and complex logic, not every possible edge case.

### 2. Tracer Bullet

Write ONE test that confirms ONE thing about the system:

```
RED:   Write test for first behavior → test fails
GREEN: Write minimal code to pass → test passes
```

This is your tracer bullet - proves the path works end-to-end.

### 3. Incremental Loop

For each remaining behavior:

```
RED:   Write next test → fails
GREEN: Minimal code to pass → passes
```

Rules:

- One test at a time
- Only enough code to pass current test
- Don't anticipate future tests
- Keep tests focused on observable behavior

### 4. Refactor

After all tests pass, look for [refactor candidates](refactoring.md):

- [ ] Extract duplication
- [ ] Deepen modules (move complexity behind simple interfaces)
- [ ] Apply SOLID principles where natural
- [ ] Consider what new code reveals about existing code
- [ ] Run tests after each refactor step

**Never refactor while RED.** Get to GREEN first.

## Checklist Per Cycle

```
[ ] Test describes behavior, not implementation
[ ] Test uses public interface only
[ ] Test would survive internal refactor
[ ] Code is minimal for this test
[ ] No speculative features added
```

Use top-level `import type` declarations for type-only dependencies. NEVER write `import("pkg").Type` inside source annotations.

## Why

- Top-level imports expose dependencies immediately.
- Import sorting and deduplication can manage them.
- Signatures stay readable and reviewable.
- Re-exports do not inherit noisy inline paths.

## Avoid

```typescript
// Bad — inline imports hide dependencies in signatures.
function run(client: import("some-sdk").Client, input: import("arktype").infer<Schema>): Promise<Output>;

// Bad — annotations become path dumps.
const options: import("some-sdk/config").ClientOptions = { ... };
```

## Use

```typescript
import type { Client } from "some-sdk";
import type { ClientOptions } from "some-sdk/config";
import type { infer as Infer } from "arktype";

function run(client: Client, input: Infer<Schema>): Promise<Output>;
const options: ClientOptions = { ... };
```

## Exceptions

- Ambient `.d.ts` globals that must not become modules.
- Generated files whose generator owns import management.

In normal `.ts` / `.tsx` source, use `import type`.

# Integrated Action Plan: tau v18.2.8 Configuration, Upstream Fix Verification, and Ranch Ecosystem Restructuring

This report integrates every finding from the pasted content, the current log, and upstream issue/PR verification. It corrects the flailing model's mistakes, resolves the `ffs -t` mystery, and gives you a grounded, executable plan.

---

## Part 0: Upstream Issue & PR Verification (The “Hoisted Developers” Test)

Before touching `.tau`, we verify what the upstream projects actually accepted, merged, or rejected. This is the "test PRs or issues" step.

| Item | Status | What It Means for tau |
|---|---|---|
| **earendil-works/pi Issue #918** | **Closed** — issue #918 was closed in favor of PR #917 | The bug is real and documented. The fix lives in PR #917. |
| **earendil-works/pi PR #917** | **Reopened after auto-close** — initially closed by contributor bot, then maintainer `badlogic` reopened it and said "Will take a bit to review it". The fix adds a `.done` handler and prefers accumulated arguments over empty `{}` from `output_item.done`. | **tau v18.2.8 must be checked** to see if this PR landed. If it did not, tool calls with GLM-4.7-Flash on LM Studio will fail with `must have required property 'command'`. |
| **can1357/oh-my-pi Issue #1991** | **Open** — the Todo tool schema mismatch is documented: Zod schema defines `list` as `z.array(z.string())` but docs imply `z.array(z.object({phase, items}))`. | tau v18.2.8 inherits this bug. The `todo.md` docs confirm the **correct** format: `list: { phase: string; items: string[] }[]`. |
| **earendil-works/pi Issue #2745** | **Fixed on main** — the same class of bug (`.done` handler not emitting a stream event) was fixed in `openai-responses-shared.ts`. | This confirms the pattern: OpenAI-compatible endpoints that send arguments in a single `.done` event need explicit handling. |
| **vLLM GLM-4.7 tool parser PRs** | **Open/rejected** — PR #54971, #51364, #37386 are open or rejected. These are **vLLM** parser fixes, not Pi fixes. | Not directly relevant to tau, but shows the GLM-4.7 tool-calling ecosystem is fragmented. |
| **pi-tool-repair extension** | **Available** — a validate-then-repair extension that fixes common LLM tool-call mistakes before execution. | Could be a fallback if tau cannot patch the provider layer. |

**Bottom line:** The upstream fix for the GLM-4.7 `.done` bug exists in PR #917, but its merge status into a tagged release is not visible from the search results. You must check tau’s git history.

---

## Part 1: The GLM-4.7-Flash Tool-Calling Bug — Integrated Fix

### What the pasted content said (and what’s correct)
> “The provider sends tool call arguments via `response.function_call_arguments.done` events instead of streaming them via `response.function_call_arguments.delta` events. The final `response.output_item.done` event therefore contains empty `{}` arguments, and validation fails.”

**Confirmed by Issue #918** — the provider (LM Studio hosting GLM-4.7-Flash) sends the full arguments in a single `.done` event. Pi only handled `.delta`, so the final `output_item.done` arrived with empty `{}` arguments. The fix (PR #917) adds a `.done` handler and prefers the accumulated arguments.

### Verification command for tau
```bash
cd /path/to/tau
git log --oneline --all | grep -i "function_call_arguments.done\|call arguments done"
# Or search the source:
rg -n "function_call_arguments.done" packages/ai/src/
```

### If tau does NOT have the fix
**Option A — Cherry-pick PR #917:**
```bash
git remote add upstream https://github.com/earendil-works/pi.git 2>/dev/null || true
git fetch upstream
git cherry-pick <commit-sha-from-PR-917>
```

**Option B — Use a different provider for tool-heavy sessions.** The log shows tau using `cloudflare-ai-gateway/workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash`. Cloudflare’s AI Gateway may normalize the event format. If tool calls work through Cloudflare but fail through LM Studio, the bug is confined to the raw LM Studio path.

**Option C — Install `pi-tool-repair` as a safety net** (Pi extension):
```bash
pi install npm:pi-tool-repair
```
This validates and repairs tool-call arguments before execution, catching the empty-`{}` case.

---

## Part 2: The Todo Schema Error — Integrated Fix

### What the pasted content said
> “The tool likely expects something like an object with a `phases` array.”

**Partially correct, but wrong format.** The actual schema from `todo.md`:

> `init` | `list` or flat `items` | `phase` (optional) | Replaces the entire list — with `list`, uses the given phases; with a flat `items` array, synthesizes one phase.

The `list` field is: `{ phase: string; items: string[] }[]` — an array of phase objects, each with a non-empty `items` array.

### The actual error in your log
The error `"list must be phased task list (init) (was a string)"` means the agent sent a **flat string**, not a structured array. This is a different failure than Issue #1991 (which is a Zod schema mismatch). The agent likely sent:

```json
{"op": "init", "list": "Step 1: Inventory, Step 2: Recover..."}
```

### Correct payload
```json
{
  "op": "init",
  "list": [
    {"phase": "Step 1 Inventory", "items": ["List all files", "Count directories"]},
    {"phase": "Step 2 Verify Claims", "items": ["Check SHAs", "Check ports", "Check systemd"]}
  ]
}
```

### Integrated fix — context file
Create `~/.tau/context/todo-schema.md`:
```markdown
# Todo Tool Schema (tau v18.2.8)

The `todo` tool `init` op requires `list` as an array of phase objects:

```json
{
  "op": "init",
  "list": [
    {"phase": "Phase Name", "items": ["task1", "task2"]}
  ]
}
```

Each `items` array must have at least 1 item. Do NOT pass a flat string.
Do NOT wrap in an `ops` array unless the tool description explicitly says so.

Available ops: init, start, done, drop, block, unblock, rm, append, view.
```

Add to `~/.tau/agent/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "contextFiles": ["~/.tau/context/todo-schema.md"]
}
```

---

## Part 3: The `ffs -t` Mystery — Resolved

### What the pasted content said
> “There’s a shell shim injecting `-t`. Let me trace where it’s coming from.”

### What’s actually true
**There was never a shim.** `ffs` is a clap-based CLI. Clap parses `-type` as the short option `-t` with the attached value `ype`. Since `ffs find` has no `-t` flag, it errors. The correct flag is `--mode`:

```bash
ffs find --mode directories projects/range
```

Valid modes: `files` (default), `directories`, `mixed`. The `--scored` flag adds role-aware ranking.

The pasted content’s 10-minute rabbit hole — checking `.bashrc`, `.bashrc.env`, `declare -f find`, `shopt extdebug`, `compgen -A function`, `strace` — was **all wasted effort on a problem that didn’t exist**.

### Integrated fix — two layers

**Layer 1 — Context file** (`~/.tau/context/ffs-syntax.md`):
```markdown
# ffs CLI Reference

`ffs` is NOT `find(1)`. It uses clap and long-form flags.

| Task | Correct | Wrong |
|---|---|---|
| Search directories | `ffs find --mode directories <needle>` | `ffs find -type d` |
| Search files | `ffs find --mode files <needle>` | `ffs find -type f` |
| Search both | `ffs find --mode mixed <needle>` | — |
| Role-ranked results | `ffs find --scored <needle>` | — |

Do NOT use `-type`. It parses as `-t` + `ype` and errors.
```

**Layer 2 — `tool_call` rewrite hook** (`~/.tau/agent/extensions/ffs-syntax-fixer/index.ts`):
```typescript
export default function(pi) {
  pi.on("tool_call", async (event) => {
    if (event.toolName === "bash") {
      const cmd = String(event.input.command ?? "");
      const fixed = cmd
        .replace(/ffs\s+find\s+(.+?)\s+-type\s+d/g, "ffs find --mode directories $1")
        .replace(/ffs\s+find\s+(.+?)\s+-type\s+f/g, "ffs find --mode files $1");
      if (fixed !== cmd) return { input: { ...event.input, command: fixed } };
    }
  });
}
```

This uses the OMP v17.1.7+ `tool_call` input-revision API: handlers can return `input` to **revise arguments**, not just block. The OMP `prepareArguments` hook also exists for normalizing raw model arguments before schema validation.

---

## Part 4: The Shell Shim Rabbit Hole — Prevention

The agent wasted ~10 minutes because it **assumed** something was injecting `-t` and never tested the simplest hypothesis (clap parsing). Add to `~/.tau/context/debugging-discipline.md`:

```markdown
# Debugging Discipline

When a CLI tool reports an unexpected argument:
1. FIRST: Read the tool's `--help` output. The flag may simply not exist.
2. SECOND: Check if the argument is a short-option cluster (e.g., `-type` → `-t ype`).
3. THIRD: Only if 1 and 2 fail, check for shell aliases/functions/wrappers.

Do NOT assume a shell shim before verifying the tool's own parser behavior.
```

---

## Part 5: Provider Budget Management (Cloudflare 403/429)

The log shows two hard failures:
- **403**: `glm-5.2` and `kimi-k2.6` not available on Workers Free plan.
- **429**: 10,000 neuron daily allocation exhausted.

### Integrated fix — provider fallback chain
Add to `~/.tau/agent/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "providers": {
    "cloudflare-ai-gateway": {
      "models": {
        "default": "@cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash",
        "verification": "@cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash"
      },
      "fallback": {
        "on403": "openrouter",
        "on429": "local"
      }
    }
  },
  "fallbackProviders": {
    "openrouter": {

    },

    }
  }

```

The `local` fallback routes to `herd` (your Go daemon on `:25100`), which is the whole point of the ranch ecosystem — local inference as a safety net.

---

## Part 6: Finding Community Issues — Integrated Tooling

### What the pasted content said
> “There is no single built-in tool. You add it via an extension like pi-mini-web-research (GitHub issue search via gh) or an MCP server like ZRead.”

### What’s actually true
**pi-mini-web-research** provides a `github` tool that searches repos, code, and issues via the `gh` CLI. Zero npm dependencies, Python stdlib only.

**ZRead MCP** provides `search_doc` for searching GitHub repo docs, issues, PRs, and contributors. Exclusive to GLM Coding Plan users.

**Option B — ZRead MCP (requires Z.AI API key):**

export ZAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
cat > ~/.tau/agent/mcp.json << 'EOF'
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "zread": {

## Part 3: The `ffs -t` Mystery — Resolved

### What the pasted content said
> “There’s a shell shim injecting `-t`. Let me trace where it’s coming from.”

### What’s actually true
**There was never a shim.** `ffs` is a clap-based CLI. Clap parses `-type` as the short option `-t` with the attached value `ype`. Since `ffs find` has no `-t` flag, it errors. The correct flag is `--mode`:

```bash
ffs find --mode directories projects/range
```

Valid modes: `files` (default), `directories`, `mixed`. The `--scored` flag adds role-aware ranking.

The pasted content’s 10-minute rabbit hole — checking `.bashrc`, `.bashrc.env`, `declare -f find`, `shopt extdebug`, `compgen -A function`, `strace` — was **all wasted effort on a problem that didn’t exist**.

### Integrated fix — two layers

**Layer 1 — Context file** (`~/.tau/context/ffs-syntax.md`):
```markdown
# ffs CLI Reference

`ffs` is NOT `find(1)`. It uses clap and long-form flags.

| Task | Correct | Wrong |
|---|---|---|
| Search directories | `ffs find --mode directories <needle>` | `ffs find -type d` |
| Search files | `ffs find --mode files <needle>` | `ffs find -type f` |
| Search both | `ffs find --mode mixed <needle>` | — |
| Role-ranked results | `ffs find --scored <needle>` | — |

Do NOT use `-type`. It parses as `-t` + `ype` and errors.
```

**Layer 2 — `tool_call` rewrite hook** (`~/.tau/agent/extensions/ffs-syntax-fixer/index.ts`):
```typescript
export default function(pi) {
  pi.on("tool_call", async (event) => {
    if (event.toolName === "bash") {
      const cmd = String(event.input.command ?? "");
      const fixed = cmd
        .replace(/ffs\s+find\s+(.+?)\s+-type\s+d/g, "ffs find --mode directories $1")
        .replace(/ffs\s+find\s+(.+?)\s+-type\s+f/g, "ffs find --mode files $1");
      if (fixed !== cmd) return { input: { ...event.input, command: fixed } };
    }
  });
}
```

This uses the OMP v17.1.7+ `tool_call` input-revision API: handlers can return `input` to **revise arguments**, not just block. The OMP `prepareArguments` hook also exists for normalizing raw model arguments before schema validation.

## Part 3: The `ffs -t` Mystery — Resolved

### What the pasted content said
> “There’s a shell shim injecting `-t`. Let me trace where it’s coming from.”

### What’s actually true
**There was never a shim.** `ffs` is a clap-based CLI. Clap parses `-type` as the short option `-t` with the attached value `ype`. Since `ffs find` has no `-t` flag, it errors. The correct flag is `--mode`:

```bash
ffs find --mode directories projects/range
```

Valid modes: `files` (default), `directories`, `mixed`. The `--scored` flag adds role-aware ranking.

The pasted content’s 10-minute rabbit hole — checking `.bashrc`, `.bashrc.env`, `declare -f find`, `shopt extdebug`, `compgen -A function`, `strace` — was **all wasted effort on a problem that didn’t exist**.

### Integrated fix — two layers

**Layer 1 — Context file** (`~/.tau/context/ffs-syntax.md`):
```markdown
# ffs CLI Reference

`ffs` is NOT `find(1)`. It uses clap and long-form flags.

| Task | Correct | Wrong |
|---|---|---|
| Search directories | `ffs find --mode directories <needle>` | `ffs find -type d` |
| Search files | `ffs find --mode files <needle>` | `ffs find -type f` |
| Search both | `ffs find --mode mixed <needle>` | — |
| Role-ranked results | `ffs find --scored <needle>` | — |

Do NOT use `-type`. It parses as `-t` + `ype` and errors.
```

**Layer 2 — `tool_call` rewrite hook** (`~/.tau/agent/extensions/ffs-syntax-fixer/index.ts`):
```typescript
export default function(pi) {
  pi.on("tool_call", async (event) => {
    if (event.toolName === "bash") {
      const cmd = String(event.input.command ?? "");
      const fixed = cmd
        .replace(/ffs\s+find\s+(.+?)\s+-type\s+d/g, "ffs find --mode directories $1")
        .replace(/ffs\s+find\s+(.+?)\s+-type\s+f/g, "ffs find --mode files $1");
      if (fixed !== cmd) return { input: { ...event.input, command: fixed } };
    }
  });
}
```

This uses the OMP v17.1.7+ `tool_call` input-revision API: handlers can return `input` to **revise arguments**, not just block. The OMP `prepareArguments` hook also exists for normalizing raw model arguments before schema validation.

Across all ten patterns, the failure has the same shape:

> **The agent produces the *form* of work (reasoning blocks, tool calls, todo updates) without producing the *substance* (reading files it claims to read, testing hypotheses it claims to form, respecting policies it claims to follow).**

**It's an execution failure that masquerades as reasoning.** The model has enough capacity to *know* what to do. It lacks the discipline to *do it* without re-narrating the plan every turn.

## What to Actually Do

You asked for a Pareto-focused prompt earlier. That's the wrong shape. Pareto won't fix this because Pareto is still a composite reasoning system. What you need is one of:

1. **A tighter harness.** Constrain the agent so that "read a file" produces an *expanded* view, not a truncated one. The `251 more lines` collapse is where half the flailing originates.

2. **A rule that bans the "We need to X" phrasing.** Force the agent to commit to a single tool call per turn and observe the result before writing its next 500-word plan.

5. **A rule that requires the agent to name the file it's about to read *and then actually read it to completion* before proposing an edit.** The current agent reads 3 lines, truncates, and then proposes edits to line 147.

The flailing is structural. Fix the harness and the model stops flailing. Fix the model and the harness stays broken.

# Tau Rebranding Plan

## Context
The repository is a fork of an upstream project (oh-my-pi) but still carries upstream identity in the compiled binary, help output, banners, error messages, and internal package references. The goal is to rebrand the fork to present "toxicwind" identity in all user-visible strings and ensure internal dependencies no longer reference upstream names where they live inside the repo.

## Approach
1. Identify all user-visible strings that contain upstream identity (e.g., "oh-my-pi", "omp", "pi-") in source code, templates, and configuration files.
2. Replace these strings with appropriate toxicwind/tau equivalents, preserving functionality.
3. Update internal package references (imports, package.json names) for any packages that live inside the monorepo and carry upstream identity.
4. Ensure the compiled binary reports the correct version and name via --version and --help.
5. Remove any symlinks that could preserve backward compatibility.
6. Verify changes by building the binary and checking its output.

## Critical files & anchors

<critical>
Plan mode active.
- Working tree/system read-only: NEVER create, edit, delete, or rename working-tree files; NEVER run state-changing commands (`git commit`, `npm install`, migrations) or otherwise change the system.
- `local://`: session-local planning artifacts; MAY create/update only when explicitly requested or needed for the plan; NEVER delete/rename.
- Canonical plan: MUST write `local://<slug>-plan.md`.

Implementing: write the plan `<slug>`/title, plain text, to `xd://propose` with `write`; `<slug>` MUST match `local://<slug>-plan.md`, allowed characters: letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens. User then selects an execution option; full write access restored.

NEVER ask user to exit plan mode or request approval in prose/with `ask`; approval ONLY via `xd://propose` write.
</critical>

## What a plan is

Plan: execution spec, not design doc. Approval may clear/compact the conversation; another engineer/fresh agent implements solely from the file. A competent implementer unfamiliar with the conversation MUST execute top-to-bottom with ZERO design decisions; file contains every choice.

Detail removes implementer decisions, not padding. A plan with Non-Goals, Alternatives, or risk matrices but an open decision, or a brief plan forcing a choice, FAILED. Decision-completeness > brevity.

## Plan file

Existing plan: `local://tau-rebrand-plan.md`; read, incrementally update with `edit`. Different task → retain it; create `local://<slug>-plan.md`.

`edit`: incremental edits only. `write`: create/full replacement only. MUST record findings as learned; NEVER defer all writing to the end.
## Ground every claim

Resolve unknowns by discovery, not questions.

- Discoverable facts — locations, behavior, signatures, configs: MUST discover with `glob`, `grep`, `read`, or parallel `scout` subagents (via `task`). Every asserted path, symbol, signature, behavior: actually read this session. Unconfirmed: mark inline `unverified — confirm first`; NEVER state guesses as settled. Ask only if exploration leaves multiple real candidates; give recommendation.
- Preferences/tradeoffs — intent, UX, scope edges, performance vs. simplicity: not code-derivable. Ask early via `ask`: 2–4 mutually exclusive options + recommended default. Unanswered → use default; record under Assumptions.

Every question MUST alter plan or resolve load-bearing choice; batch. NEVER ask what exploration answers or filler.
## Workflow — parallel

<procedure>
1. **Understand** — request and supporting code. Scope spans areas → parallel `scout` subagents via `task`, distinct focuses: implementations, related components, test patterns. Find reusable code before proposing new.
2. **Design** — draft approach from findings, briefly weigh tradeoffs, commit. Large/cross-cutting → MAY spawn critique subagent before commitment.
3. **Review** — read intended files; validate approach against code and literal request; `ask` resolves remaining preferences.
4. **Write** — plan per **Plan contents**.
</procedure>

## Plan contents

Scannable markdown; depth follows change: one-file fix → few bullets; cross-cutting change → ordered behavior steps.

- **Context** — literal ask, need, intended end state; 2–4 sentences. Every requested outcome maps to a step; add nothing beyond ask.
- **Approach** — load-bearing ordered change steps. Order for a building tree and passing existing tests after each; state dependencies and independencies. Group by behavior, NEVER file. Each step:
  - Concrete edit: verb, exact target, new behavior; NEVER merely area to “update”/“handle”.
  - Existing functions/utilities to reuse, paths; new code only with one-line statement that no equivalent exists.
  - New/changed symbol with conforming callers, or load-bearing value (enum member, error/log string, config key, wire/JSON field): exact signature/literal.
  - Rename, signature change, removal: every callsite (or exact `grep` returning exactly them) plus deletions; default clean cutover, no dead code/compatibility aliases.
  - Rival patterns: copy and avoid named.
  - Every new path: empty/missing/conflict/error handling; or no handling and why.
- **Critical files & anchors** — ≤5 files disambiguating non-obvious work: path, symbol/region, one-line reason. Line numbers hints; implementer rereads before edit. Omit Approach-obvious files.
- **Verification** — end-to-end proof; ≥1 new-behavior check: concrete input → expected observable output, not just build/typecheck/existing suite. Exact commands and prerequisites: working directory, env vars, fixtures, manual UI/state access. Tie risky-step checks to steps.
- **Assumptions & contingencies** — only user-overridable decisions. NEVER put implementer decisions here; they belong in Approach. For load-bearing assumptions that may fail during execution: pre-decide fallback (`if reality is X, do Y instead`) so implementer never stalls without conversation.

Cut decision-free material: restated invariants, unaffected behavior, mechanical repetition, narration. Specify what implementer would otherwise invent.

<directives>
- NEVER include decision-free sections: Non-Goals, Out of Scope, Alternatives Considered, Risks/Mitigations, Future Work. Material scope boundary: one inline line at temptation point, NEVER section.
- NEVER plan mechanical cleanup tail: changelog/release notes, doc updates, formatter/linter runs, scaffold removal. These run automatically after working change; no planning. Behavior-defining tests/end-to-end proof are not cleanup: retain in **Verification**.
- NEVER reference planning conversation (`the option we chose above`, `as discussed`); unavailable to reader. State choice/reason inline.
- NEVER invent request-unspecified schema, precedence, fallback policy, unless needed to prevent concrete implementation mistake; then state decision, not open question.
</directives>

<caution>
Review options:
- **Approve and execute** — fresh context (session cleared).
- **Approve and compact context** — discussion distilled, then executes here.
- **Approve and keep context** — executes here with exploration history.
- **Save and quit** — copies the plan to a chosen path, then starts a new session.

All require self-contained file.
</caution>

<critical>
Before approval: engineer unfamiliar with conversation can execute every step without design decision and determine success at each step. Otherwise deepen any choice-forcing or ambiguous-done step.

Turn ends ONLY:
1. `ask` gathers requirements/chooses approaches; OR
2. `write` writes plan `<slug>`/title as plain text to `xd://propose` (`local://<slug>-plan.md` slug).

NEVER request plan approval via prose/`ask`; MUST use `xd://propose` write. MUST continue until decision-complete.
</critical>

# Vibecoding General — Multi-Agent Coding Orchestration

Design-first, multi-agent workflow for building general software projects. Covers Python tools, data pipelines, ML systems, APIs, games, bots, CLI apps, mobile apps, and any non-frontend coding task.

## Core Principles

1. **Spec-first.** A specification document (`SPEC.md`) is written before any implementation. It is the single source of truth for architecture, modules, interfaces, and data flow.
2. **Spec fidelity.** Subagents implement SPEC.md faithfully — exact interfaces, exact module boundaries, exact data formats. No unilateral changes.
3. **Main agent owns init, merge, integration.** Subagents implement and commit on their branches.
4. **Parallelism by modules & features.** Each subagent owns one or more modules/features. Group related work into one agent to minimize cross-agent dependencies.
5. **Git worktrees isolate work.** Each subagent works in its own git worktree to avoid conflicts. The shared repo is the coordination hub.
6. **Interface contracts are sacred.** Define function signatures, data schemas, and file formats in the spec. Subagents implement to these contracts so modules integrate cleanly.
7. **Test before merge.** Each subagent runs tests for their module before committing. Main agent runs integration tests after merge.

## Mode Selection

|Condition|Mode|
|---|---|
|Task has 3+ distinct modules or components|**Mode A** (multi-agent)|
|Task involves both infrastructure and application logic|**Mode A** (multi-agent)|
|Task is a full system (API + workers + data pipeline, etc.)|**Mode A** (multi-agent)|
|Task is a single script, tool, or focused feature|**Mode B** (single agent)|
|Task is a bug fix or small enhancement|**Mode B** (single agent)|
|When in doubt|**Mode B** (single agent)|

---

## Worktree Reference

Git worktrees allow multiple agents to work on the same repo simultaneously without conflicts.

### Setup (each subagent)
```bash
cd /mnt/agents/output/project                         # shared repo
git worktree add $HOME/work-<branch> <branch>     # create local worktree
cd $HOME/work-<branch>                            # work here
```

### Rules
- Each subagent MUST use a unique worktree path (`$HOME/work-<branch>`).
- **Never run `git worktree prune`** — it destroys other agents' worktree entries.
- Never work directly in `/mnt/agents/output/project` — always use a worktree.
- After committing in a worktree, the main agent merges from the shared repo.

### Cleanup (main agent, after all merges complete)
```bash
cd /mnt/agents/output/project
git worktree remove $HOME/work-<branch>   # optional, per branch
```

---

## File Layout

```
/mnt/agents/output/
├── SPEC.md                        # Project specification (single source of truth)
├── info.md                        # Research findings (if applicable)
├── project/                       # Shared git repo (coordination hub)
│   ├── .git/
│   └── ...                        # Project structure per SPEC.md
│
$HOME/work-<branch>/               # Local worktree (unique per subagent)
└── ...                            # Same structure, isolated working copy
```
